common.noDecisionBody: The technologies below are under evaluation through MoUs and studies. None of these MoUs is a deployment decision, and this page contains no projected headcount and no site information.

horizonHint.prepare: skills useful now, for work ENEC already does

pub.intro: ENEC launched the ADVANCE programme to evaluate small modular reactors, advanced reactors and microreactors. Here is what those technologies are and which skills they may need.
pub.advanceLaunchBody: ENEC launched ADVANCE to evaluate SMRs, advanced reactors and microreactors for the UAE and abroad.
pub.copBody: MoUs with GE Hitachi, TerraPower, Westinghouse, X-energy, USNC, MoltexFLEX and CNNC; others followed in later years.
pub.fanrBody: FANR said it had received no formal proposal for new capacity and was training its staff on SMRs.
pub.techDesc: General descriptions for orientation. Each cites its MoU source and date.
pub.techFoot: Technology families are general descriptions. None of these MoUs is a deployment decision.
pub.matrixDesc: How each skill area relates to today's APR-1400 work at Barakah.
pub.bridgeDesc: Pick a current role to see what transfers to a technology and what is new.
pub.noBridges: No bridges for this role yet.
pub.roleLink: Open this role in the career map
pub.catalogueDesc: Concept roles that these technologies could need. Descriptions only: no numbers, no sites, no dates.
pub.catalogueFoot: Concept roles for career conversations. They are not vacancies and imply no plan to hire.
pub.tracksDesc: Advanced reactor fundamentals for interested staff and students.
pub.aiBody: The ENEC-KEPCO AI Innovation Lab (MoU, Nov 2025) and the ENECIQ agentic AI platform co-developed with Presight, which runs separately from reactor systems.
pub.cmBody: Exploratory only: letters of intent and research cooperation on hydrogen and related systems. No pilot or investment decision has been announced.
pub.guard: A public payload check flagged content on this page for review.

tech.sourceFoot: MoUs record intentions to evaluate; they are not deployment decisions.

wf.intro: Compare a scenario's demand for future skills with today's readiness, then plan actions. Every index here is SIMULATED.
wf.simBody: Indices run from 0 to 100 and are illustrative. They are not forecasts, not headcounts and not decisions. Use them to discuss options.
wf.adoptionHint: Scales the scenario's demand index from half to one and a half times.
wf.gapDesc: Gap = demand index minus readiness index. High is 30 or more.
wf.plansDesc: Actions HR has recorded against SIMULATED scenarios. Each save is audited.
wf.ownerHint: A role, not a person (for example: Nuclear Training).
wf.planNote: Plans respond to a SIMULATED scenario. They are not commitments to hire or deploy.
wf.savePlanBody: The action is saved and written to the audit log.
wf.structureDesc: How many current roles have a mapped skill bridge into each technology, and how many concept roles exist.
wf.scnAHint: Evaluation continues at today's pace; consulting and governed AI lead.
wf.scnBHint: A light-water SMR option leads; advanced coolants recede.
wf.suppressedHint: Suppressed: fewer than 10 people. Readiness is at most {max}.
wf.gapDescComputed: Readiness is computed from the skills catalogue: the share of active staff at the target level on each key's catalogue skills (transfers and new count in full, adapts at half). Gap = demand minus readiness; ≥ marks a lower bound where readiness is suppressed.
wf.radarNote: Dashed line: the other scenario's demand. Axes marked (<10) have suppressed readiness and are drawn at zero.
wf.statPopulationSub: Active staff with a skills profile
wf.statSuppressedSub: Fewer than 10 people: no value shown
wf.assumptionsDesc: Each demand index rests on a written assumption with public sources. The chip shows the change against the other scenario.
wf.familyDesc: {shown} of {total} families have 10 or more measured staff; the rest are suppressed.
wf.familyNote: Security, safeguards and cyber families are never broken out (career-path level only).
wf.plansDescKeyed: Actions HR has recorded against SIMULATED scenarios. Each action is keyed to a catalogue skill; the radar label is kept. Each save is audited.

why.population: Population: {n} active staff with a skills profile.
why.transfers: {skill} at level {level} or above counts in full (transfers, ×{credit}).
why.adapts: {skill} at level {level} or above counts at half (adapts, ×{credit}).
why.new: {skill} at level {level} or above counts in full (the new capability, ×{credit}).
why.suppressed: Fewer than {min} people qualify, so the value is suppressed (at most {max}).

IAEA-WFP.name: IAEA NG-T-3.10 Workforce Planning and the Nuclear Infrastructure Competency Framework
IAEA-WFP.borrow: Scenario bands rather than point estimates, a fill plan per gap, and a "why this competency exists" link to its activity.
IAEA-WFP.applied: Demand is shown per scenario with its assumption and sources, readiness is assessed from today's staff, and every gap has a plan action keyed to a catalogue skill.

ESCO.name: ESCO v1.2.1 (European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations)
ESCO.borrow: Reusability level on every skill, Arabic preferred and alternative labels, obsolete-not-deleted, and a published crosswalk.
ESCO.applied: One keyspace: every future-skill key resolves to a catalogue skill, map rows are switched off rather than deleted, and the crosswalk downloads as CSV.

ks.intro: One keyspace for future skills. Every ADVANCE skill, radar key and gap-plan key resolves to at least one skill in the Kafa'a catalogue, with how today's skill carries over and the level that counts.
ks.statAdvSub: as-* keys with a catalogue skill
ks.allResolvedBody: ADVANCE skills, radar keys and gap plans all join the skills catalogue, so readiness can be computed from people's skill records.
ks.creditTitle: How a catalogue skill counts toward readiness

relCredit.transfers: carries over as it is: counts in full
relCredit.adapts: familiar but works differently: counts at half
relCredit.new: names the new capability itself: counts in full

ks.noPlansBody: Gap plans are HR records; HR analysts, the CHCO office and auditors see them.
ks.editIntro: Choose a catalogue skill to add or change for this key. Rows are never deleted: switch a row off instead. Security skills are not offered.
ks.primaryHint: Plans and the radar label resolve to the primary skill.
ks.activeHint: Switch off to stop this skill counting toward readiness.
ks.lastActive: This is the key's last active skill, so it stays on.
ks.saveBody: The change applies to readiness at once and is written to the audit log.
